name: AI after-hours answering agent for UK trades
one_liner: Set up and run AI voice agents that answer missed and after-hours calls for local trades. The agent qualifies the lead and passes urgent or high-value calls to the owner.
customer: Owners of small home-service businesses such as plumbers, electricians, HVAC, roofers and locksmiths
offer: A done-for-you AI phone receptionist: setup, script, call routing and monthly management
how_it_makes_money: Setup fee plus a monthly retainer. The transcript mentions '300 bucks a customer' but doesn't say what it covers.
startup_cost: low (uses 3-4 software tools, mostly with free trials)
time_to_first_revenue: Days. A customer said yes within 56 minutes on camera.
evidence: 'From idea to customer that said yes in under an hour' – a local business owner who didn't know the host (5mClVr2cd5U)
'Most of them are not answering their phone after hours' (5mClVr2cd5U)
'You're going to start getting customers on day two. 300 bucks a customer' (47UgXbHp6nM)
risks: Many competitors are selling the same thing
Customers may cancel if lead quality is poor
Voice AI mistakes could hurt the client's reputation
UK call-recording and GDPR compliance

name: YouTube-to-print magazine for creators
one_liner: Turn a creator's YouTube tutorials into a physical print magazine that is sold to their audience.
customer: YouTube creators with tutorial or how-to channels, and their audiences
offer: Edited, designed print magazines (one-off or subscription) made from existing video content
how_it_makes_money: Magazine sales and subscriptions, split with the creator or paid as a licence fee
startup_cost: low-medium (design, AI transcription and editing, print-on-demand)
evidence: 'He has a $7 million a year business repurposing their YouTube tutorials into physical magazine' (4JgLTWSzGgc)
risks: Only one example, mentioned briefly
You need creators to partner with or license their content
Print margins and logistics
The model depends on the creator promoting it

name: Paid snail-mail story letter subscription
one_liner: A subscription that posts two story letters a month to subscribers.
customer: Consumers, possibly gift buyers, families and nostalgia seekers
offer: Two physical story letters a month
evidence: 'They send two letters per month to people paying $10 per month that tell a story. We're talking 310 grand a month' with no paid ads, only word of mouth (3cKupknhU1w)
risks: Rising postage costs eat into margin
Growth depends on word of mouth or a creative hook
Subscribers cancel
Details of the example are thin

name: Hot tub servicing for short-term rentals
one_liner: Weekly hot tub cleaning and chemical servicing sold only to Airbnb and holiday-let owners.
customer: Short-term rental owners and holiday-let managers
offer: Recurring weekly hot tub maintenance, plus repairs and cover sales
how_it_makes_money: $50-100 per hot tub per week on a recurring contract
evidence: 'They charge between $50 and $100 a week to service these… They do 25 a day' (3cKupknhU1w)
'Austin on Twitter… hot tub maintenance business where he only services Airbnbs' (3cKupknhU1w)
risks: Done in person, so you need staff to scale
Seasonal and regional demand
UK holiday-let market is under tax and regulatory pressure

name: Custom garage shelving sold on Facebook Marketplace
one_liner: Build and install custom garage shelves, with all leads coming from Facebook Marketplace listings.
offer: Custom-measured, built and installed garage shelving
how_it_makes_money: Per-job pricing. A $1,000 shelf costs about $150 in materials, giving $15k a month in net profit.
evidence: 'Make 15 grand a month in net profit selling custom garage shelves exclusively on Facebook Marketplace' (4NJHK5KdASc)
'A $1,000 shelf, the expenses on that is probably 150 bucks' (4NJHK5KdASc)
He quit his day job in May 2024 (4NJHK5KdASc)
risks: Manual labour and in-person work
UK garages are smaller, so demand is lower
Hard to grow beyond the founder without subcontractors

name: Packaged beach/outdoor wedding service
one_liner: An all-inclusive outdoor wedding package (setup, chairs, coordination) that doesn't require owning a venue.
customer: Couples planning small outdoor or destination weddings
offer: Turnkey wedding package: location, rentals, setup and coordination
how_it_makes_money: Fixed-price packages at 100+ weddings a year
evidence: 'Started the business with $20,000. It does $3 million a year… hundred something weddings a year' (2Qh3EaMegnY)
'Outdoor weddings two-thirds of all weddings; 10 years ago it was 40%' (2Qh3EaMegnY)
risks: Delivery happens on-site
Seasonal and weather-dependent
Permits
note_founder_fit: A Portugal destination-wedding package (Algarve/Comporta) sold to UK couples would draw on the founder's UK and Portugal connections, but the founder would need local partners to deliver it.

name: Marketplace micro-apps (Shopify etc.)
one_liner: Build small single-feature apps for app marketplaces such as Shopify, where most customers come from the app store listing itself.
customer: Merchants on platforms such as Shopify
offer: A focused app that solves one feature gap
how_it_makes_money: Monthly subscription. The guest suggests charging premium prices ('$799… don't go cheap').
evidence: '75 app marketplaces… more demand than supply' (4IETgMZy1o0)
'Almost all your customers will come from that app store' (4IETgMZy1o0)
Guest (Rob Walling) has invested in 220+ software startups (4IETgMZy1o0)
risks: Evidence is weak: no specific app revenue is given
Platform dependency
Support burden

name: Attic, insulation and duct-sealing sales using subcontractors
one_liner: Sell energy-efficiency jobs (duct sealing, insulation, air scrubbers) using infrared-camera inspections, and subcontract the installation.
offer: Inspection, then installation of duct sealing, insulation or an air scrubber
how_it_makes_money: High-ticket jobs averaging about $10k. Air scrubbers sell for $1,200 and take about 30 minutes to install. The installer brings their own equipment.
evidence: 'Our average ticket is right around 10 grand' (3ywztCB-hAk)
'Subcontractor model… over a million dollars a year of net profit' (3ywztCB-hAk)
risks: Sales happen in person
The pitch relies on fear, which carries reputational risk
UK retrofit work needs installer accreditation (e.g. TrustMark/PAS 2035)
